correctness.rationale: For any finite abelian A and proper subgroup H generated by nonzero t, each triangle has a unique coset-pair sheet, each edge lies in exactly one sheet; each sheet is a connected orientable genus (m-1)(m-2)/2 surface by exact link cycles, orientation and Euler count. A connected incidence graph with 3Nd edges and d^2+3N nodes makes the whole complex homotopy equivalent to the wedge of d^2 surfaces and 3N(d-1)-d^2+1 circles. Integral homology and pi1 follow without numerical extrapolation; the package verifier independently checks small cyclic and noncyclic groups.

originality.rationale: A complete coset-normalization and graph-of-spaces homotopy classification for proper-subgroup shifts (d>=2) is not a corollary of the flabby generalized-inflation theorem, single Latin-layer wedge theorem, unit-shift two-layer integral homology theorem, or classical connected regular Latin biembeddings; each scope and implication was compared directly. Remaining risk is unindexed singular Latin-bitrade literature.
residual_risks: An older unindexed theory of separated cyclic Latin bitrades may state equivalent multi-sheet gluing and fundamental-group formulas.
The full Grannell–Knor 2010 article was not fully available; its abstract/introduction indicate a connected surface setting but a complete negative implication comparison is impossible.
All finite checks concern small groups; independent proof review and independent mathematical audit remain unperformed.

value.rationale: The classification solves a motivated proper-subgroup/nonunit-difference gap explicitly excluded by the published unit-adjacent-level result; same-face-vector examples on Z/6 distinguish a genus-ten surface, four tori plus fifteen circles and nine spheres plus twenty-eight circles. It provides exact integral homotopy, surface normalization and nonfree fundamental groups for all finite abelian groups, not just ranks or a routine parameter substitution.
